title: Turn submission + outcome (Class B — the spine lane)
description: Doc 20 §6. TurnSubmit carries the SAME Decision envelope an LlmDriver emits (AGT-A3: four drivers, one wire shape); TurnOutcome is projected from committed events emitted by commit-service.

client_request_id.description: Client-minted; the EVT-L3 idempotency triple's middle member. A retry MUST reuse it — that is what makes double-submit safe.

action.description: CWC-D6 — the contracts/agent Decision envelope by REFERENCE, not by copy: a player's UI gesture and an NPC LlmDriver's proposal are the same object, validated at the same admission gate against the same closed vocabulary (AGT-A2/A3). Duplicating the shape here would be the polyglot mirror-drift bug class.

kind.description: CWC-A6 truth-in-labeling — three DIFFERENT things the UI must not collapse: rejected = the validator said no (no turn consumed, retry free); discarded = the world moved under a valid intent (SC-A1 precondition, no turn consumed); resolved = it happened (turn consumed).

turn_number.description: DP-A17 / EVT-V4, LIVE-PROVEN in the committed log 2026-07-27: advances on `resolved` ONLY. A rejection leaves it unchanged — the client must not burn a turn slot in its UI either.

events.description: Renderable narration/effect lines derived from the committed domain events. Pre-localized (CWC-D7).

reason.description: sim-core DiscardReason — the 5-variant closed set (REC-63 as amended by REC-78).

stage.description: The admission stage that rejected (schema | idempotency | decision-vocabulary | …). Named, never generic — CS-A4: neither rejection kind is silent.

DomainEventType.description: The closed discriminant set of a committed combat fact, as it appears in the COMMITTED PAYLOAD (not on the wire — ResolvedDetail.events carries these already rendered to strings). Rust `commit-service::domain::CombatEvent` produces it; TypeScript `game-server/wire/turnOutcome.ts` consumes it, and both check against THIS rather than against each other. Added 2026-08-06 because they had no contract between them and had silently diverged 8 to 6: `status_expired` and `encounter_ended` had no consumer arm, so `renderEvent` returned undefined for facts the server really emits. NOTE THE SCOPE — this contracts the TAG SET only. The per-variant payload fields are still uncontracted, which is why this is a string enum and not an object: an object def would have to close `additionalProperties`, and closing it against a `type`-only property list would make the schema wrong for every variant that carries fields.

RefusalReason.description: M2/CMD-5 -- why a declared verb was refused. A closed ENGINE set, mirrored on both sides against THIS contract rather than against each other: FATAL-1 shipped an 8-vs-6 drift under a comment claiming the set was asserted in the tests, because the two languages were joined to one another with no contract between them.
